searches.note: Seventeen searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's; three restricted to a house's own domain (bodegachacra.com, bodeganoemia.com, familiaschroeder.com) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on one source or none was cut or hedged as the house's claim.

tested: The 1932 vineyard, the 2004 lease and later purchase, the owner who would not sell, the 1955 and 1967 vineyards, the new block from cuttings and the biodynamic certification: the house's press kits by a search restricted to bodegachacra.com, Sotheby's Wine, K&L; agreed, save the first vintage.
The first vintage: the press kit calls Treinta y Dos the first wine made at the estate, a 2008 article gives 2006 as the first vintage, Sotheby's speaks of first wines in 2003 and 2004; not settled.

The making: merchants' sheets for 2017, 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024 and a critic's note on new oak; concrete and used French oak, nine to about nineteen months, whole bunches in many vintages, no new oak since 2013.
The Mainqué Chardonnay: merchants for 2020, 2022 and 2024; oak, concrete eggs and steel, the amphora belongs to another white.

tested: 1909, General Roca, the engineer from Genoa and the professor who brought him south: Río Negro newspaper, La Nación, Forbes Argentina, Mercado; agreed. The professor is named in the family's account but not dated in two sources, so not named.
The founder's dates: two searches, none found; he is now described, not named, in the story, the house keeping its name.
The grapes he brought: the Río Negro newspaper, quoting the family; told as the family's account.
The family's line: Río Negro newspaper (a great nephew leads it) and La Nación (four generations).
Sémillon of 1942 at Finca Milagros: Forbes Argentina, Enotria, Great Wine; agreed. The Old Vineyard range a tribute to the oldest family vineyards: Natalie MacLean's review.
The making: Great Wine's notes and a merchant's note of native yeasts; no oak found in any source read.
The Riesling: Decanter, Majestic, Delectable (La Morita, 1937).

swaps.ruling: The author proposed no swap. The plan's open pick for Familia Schroeder, the Saurus Pinot Noir over a Malbec, is accepted: the house's own pages name a Saurus Patagonia Select Pinot Noir of 2003 as its first wine and Pinot Noir as its grape.

picksNoted: Fin del Mundo's Special Blend is called the flagship red by one review and the house's top level is not settled; the pick stands.
codexInTension: The library record p-bodega-chacra says the Pinot is deliberately unoaked in feel; the house ages Treinta y Dos partly in used French oak, which is not unoaked, though it has used no new oak since 2013 by one account. Reported, not edited.
